channel.title: The Retreat Register — Updates
channel.description: Verification progress from The Retreat Register, published with real numbers: coverage snapshots, data findings, and what gets cut from the register and why.

item.title: Tennessee Retreat Venues: Mountains, Music Towns, and Drive-To Reach
item.description: Smoky Mountain cabins, walkable small towns, and a huge share of the country within a day's drive - Tennessee works hard for groups.

item.title: Executive Offsite or Team Retreat? Two Different Venue Searches
item.description: The same word hides two products: boardroom privacy for a few decision-makers, or connection space for the whole team.

item.title: Bring Your Own Facilitator or Book the Venue's? How to Decide
item.description: Who runs the room changes what the venue needs to provide. A short decision rule for each path, asked before booking.

item.title: Stagger, Shuttle, or Caravan: Plan Group Arrivals Calmly
item.description: Arrival is the first session of the retreat. Three arrival models, and how to pick the one that fits the group and the venue.

item.title: How to Collect Dietary Restrictions So the Kitchen Can Deliver
item.description: Collect once, in writing, with severity flags - and get the list to the venue kitchen far enough ahead to matter.

item.title: One Big Room Is Not Enough: Plan for Breakout Spaces
item.description: The main hall photographs well, but small-group work is where most agendas actually happen - and many venues cannot host it.

item.title: The Retreat Budget Line Items First-Time Planners Forget
item.description: Lodging and food are the easy rows. The budget breaks on transport gaps, gratuities, supplies, insurance, and the missing contingency line.

item.title: Shared Rooms or Singles? Decide Before You Shortlist
item.description: Lodging configuration silently disqualifies venues. Deciding the sharing question first makes every later step honest.

item.title: Two Nights or Three? Choose the Right Retreat Length
item.description: Retreat length is a math problem: arrival and departure eat the edges, so the middle days are what the group actually buys.

item.title: How Far Ahead to Book a Retreat Venue, by Season and Group Size
item.description: Booking lead time is a sliding scale, not one magic number - peak seasons and bigger groups move it by months.

item.title: Every Outdoor Retreat Needs a Rain Plan: Build One in an Hour
item.description: The backup-space question decides whether weather cancels the agenda or just moves it indoors. Most planners ask it too late.

item.title: The Site Visit Checklist: What to Confirm Before You Sign
item.description: Listings answer the easy questions. A visit answers water pressure, walking distances, cell coverage, and how the place actually sounds.

item.title: The Attrition Clause: How to Avoid Paying for No-Shows
item.description: The contract line that bills the group for beds nobody slept in - how to find it, read it, and negotiate it before signing.

item.title: Build a Quote Comparison Sheet Before the Second Venue Replies
item.description: Venue quotes arrive in formats that refuse to line up. A one-page sheet normalizes them before memory starts filling the gaps.

item.title: How to Write a Venue Inquiry Email That Gets Comparable Answers
item.description: One well-built inquiry email, sent to every venue on the list, turns a pile of mismatched replies into a clean comparison.

item.title: What Happens at a Silent Retreat (and Who Should Book One)
item.description: No talking, no phone, no icebreakers — one of the register's rising trend terms, explained before you book one by accident.

item.title: How to Pick a Glamping Venue That Works for a Group Retreat
item.description: Canvas and stars, yes — but bathrooms, weather plans, and a real meeting space decide whether glamping works for a team.

item.title: Why Planners Are Booking Farm and Ranch Retreats in 2026
item.description: Agritourism is one of the register's fastest-climbing trend terms. What working farms and ranches give a group that resorts can't fake.

item.title: How to Choose Between Virginia's Coastal, Mountain, and Historic Venues
item.description: Blue Ridge quiet within a tank of gas of half the East Coast — and somehow still not the default.

item.title: Find More Retreat Space for Your Budget in Texas
item.description: Hill country estates, working ranches, coastal buyouts — the retreat state that out-delivers its price tag.
